slides.title: Computer science as problem solving
slides.slide: L1 Basic · Computer science as problem solving
slides.notes: Name what makes a problem suitable for a computer, such as clear steps and repeated work. Notes: ask learners how they would find the tallest person in a room; they describe each step in words. No devices are needed, just a clear list.

slides.title: Algorithms and flowcharts
slides.notes: Describe an algorithm as a flowchart and trace it by hand. Notes: draw a flowchart that finds the larger of two numbers, then run it with 7 and 4 and with 5 and 5. Learners say what the chart does when numbers are equal. Work on paper first.

slides.title: Functions and control flow
slides.slide: L3 Foundation · Functions and control flow
slides.notes: Write a function with conditions and loops and test it with chosen inputs. Notes: write a factorial function; 5 factorial must give 120, and 0 factorial must give 1. Learners test one normal case, one edge case and one wrong input. Take screen breaks.

slides.title: Data structures and binary search
slides.slide: L4 Practitioner · Data structures and binary search
slides.notes: Apply stacks, queues and sorted arrays to solve a task and predict the cost. Notes: a sorted list of 1,000 items needs at most 10 binary-search steps, since 2 to the 10 is 1,024. Learners trace a search for 37 in a list of 16 numbers and count the steps.

slides.title: Recursion and analysis
slides.notes: Analyse a recursive function, count its calls and improve it with memoisation. Notes: a naive Fibonacci of 5 makes 15 calls. Learners draw the call tree, spot repeated work, add a cache and show the calls falling to 9. Test with small inputs before large ones.

slides.title: Complexity and proofs
slides.notes: Evaluate algorithms by growth rate and prove a simple correctness claim. Notes: for n of 1,000,000, n squared is 10 to the 12, but n log2 n is about 2 times 10 to the 7. Learners prove a loop invariant for insertion sort and state the best and worst cases.

slides.title: Lower bounds and research design
slides.slide: L7 Super expert · Lower bounds and research design
slides.notes: Evaluate limits of computation and design a rigorous experiment on algorithms. Notes: any comparison sort of 10 items needs at least the ceiling of log2 of 10 factorial, which is 22 comparisons. Learners plan benchmarks with controlled inputs, repeats, confidence intervals and a data-sharing statement.
